Perfect. After Ne5+ Kh6 (or any king move), Rxd8 wins the rook. Even if Black plays Bxe5, White recaptures Rxd8 and still wins the exchange (rook for knight). This is a classic fork—the knight checks the king and attacks the undefended rook simultaneously.

**Best move:** Ne5+

**Main line:** 1. Ne5+ Kh6 (or Kh7, Kg7, Kf6) 2. Rxd8

**Motif:** fork

**Coaching note (78 words):**

When your knight lands with check, look for what else it attacks. Here, Ne5+ forks the king and the undefended rook on d8. The king must move (no piece can block), and then you capture the rook for free. This fork pattern—a checking move that also attacks a loose piece—is one of the most common tactical motifs at every level. After winning the exchange, you'll have a winning endgame.
